newsitem.title: USA: Foreclosure activity in Calif. edges up in July.
newsitem.headline: Foreclosure activity in Calif. edges up in July.

text.p: Foreclosure activity in California edged up in July as lenders moved to clear more of their backlog of delinquent mortgage loans, a real estate information service said on Tuesday.

Lending institutions started foreclosure proceedings on 13,043 homeowners last month, up 11.2 percent from 11,733 in June and up 30.5 percent from 9,998 for July a year ago, according to DataQuick Information Systems.
Last month's figure was still well below the all-time high last March of 15,473, DataQuick said.
So far this year, 97,119 California homeowners have been drawn into the foreclosure process, up 29.2 percent from 75,164 in the first seven months of last year, DataQuick said.

"The state's recovering real estate market still has areas of distress. Many of the entry-level home markets that were especially active six years ago are problem areas today," said Donald Cohn, DataQuick chief executive officer. "Although the worst is behind us, we'll have significant foreclosure levels well into next year if current trends stay in place."

So far this year, foreclosure activity has increased the most in California's Central Valley, while the increase has been nominal along the central coast and in Santa Clara and San Bernardino counties.

Santa Clara has had high sales volume during the past year that has absorbed distressed properties. San Bernardino County experienced its foreclosure surge before many other parts of the state, DataQuick said.
DataQuick monitors real estate activity nationwide.
